question: Which type of seam is most suitable for sheer fabrics to prevent seam allowances from showing through to the right side?
options: A. French seam
B. Lapped seam
C. Flat-felled seam
D. Welt seam

question: When drafting a basic bodice block, which measurement is used to determine the chest line placement?
options: A. Half the back length measurement
B. One quarter of the bust measurement plus ease
C. The armscye depth measurement
D. The shoulder slope measurement

question: A fabric with a twill weave structure will characteristically show which of the following features?
options: A. A checkerboard pattern with equal interlacings
B. Diagonal lines running at an angle across the fabric surface
C. Loops of yarn standing up from a flat base
D. Alternating floats of warp and weft yarns of equal length

question: Which fibre property is most directly responsible for wool's natural ability to resist wrinkling?
options: A. High moisture regain
B. Crimp and elasticity of the fibre
C. Low thermal conductivity
D. Hydrophobic outer scale layer

question: During the construction of a tailored jacket, pad stitching is used primarily to:
options: A. Secure the lining to the outer fabric permanently
B. Shape and stiffen the canvas interfacing to the desired roll
C. Attach the collar to the neckline with invisible stitches
D. Reinforce the pocket welts against stress

question: The term 'ease' in garment construction refers to:
options: A. The process of shrinking fabric before cutting
B. The additional fabric allowance beyond body measurements for comfort and movement
C. A technique used to join curved seams to straight edges
D. The reduction in stitch tension when sewing stretch fabrics

question: Which finishing process applied to cotton fabric gives it a permanent lustrous appearance by treating it with a caustic soda solution under tension?
options: A. Calendering
B. Singeing
C. Mercerization
D. Bleaching

question: A pattern instruction to 'stay-stitch' a curved neckline edge requires stitching:
options: A. Along the seamline with a basting stitch before cutting
B. Just inside the seamline through a single layer immediately after cutting
C. Through both fabric layers with a reinforcement stitch after assembly
D. Along the fold line to prevent stretching during pressing

question: When grading a pattern between sizes, the grade is distributed between which reference points?
options: A. Centre front, centre back, side seams and shoulder seams
B. Armhole, waistline and hemline only
C. Grain lines and fold lines exclusively
D. The dart legs and ease allowance points

question: Nylon fibres are produced through which manufacturing process?
options: A. Wet spinning of a cellulose xanthate solution
B. Melt spinning of a polyamide polymer
C. Dry spinning of an acetate solution
D. Solvent spinning of an acrylic copolymer

question: Which type of interfacing requires heat activation to bond it to the fashion fabric?
options: A. Woven sew-in interfacing
B. Non-woven sew-in interfacing
C. Fusible interfacing
D. Organza underlining

question: The drape quality of a fabric is most influenced by which combination of factors?
options: A. Fibre length and yarn twist only
B. Fabric weight, flexibility and the way threads interact in the structure
C. Thread count and selvedge width exclusively
D. Dye type and finishing chemical applied

question: A princess-line seam construction differs from a standard dart because it:
options: A. Uses a gathering technique to control fullness rather than folding
B. Replaces the dart with a continuous curved seam from shoulder or armhole to hem providing shape and seaming simultaneously
C. Is sewn on the right side of the garment as a decorative feature
D. Requires a separate facing piece to finish all its edges

question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the bias grain of a woven fabric?
options: A. It runs parallel to the selvedge and has the greatest strength
B. It runs perpendicular to the selvedge and has moderate stretch
C. It runs at a 45-degree angle to both warp and weft and has maximum stretch and drape
D. It runs diagonally at 30 degrees and is used for reinforcing stress points

question: When applying a decorative smocking stitch, the fabric must first be prepared by:
options: A. Applying a fusible interfacing to the wrong side to stabilise pleats
B. Gathering the fabric evenly using a pleating template or transfer dots so that the fabric is reduced to approximately one third of its original width
C. Cutting the fabric on the bias to allow the design to stretch outward
D. Pressing sharp knife pleats at regular intervals and basting them flat
